subtopics.title: variables
subtopics.teaching: Teach variables as named program state. Distinguish declaration, initialization, reassignment, and reading the current value; emphasize that an update changes later computations but not earlier ones.
subtopics.worked_example: If score=12, then score=score+5 and score=score*2 produces 34. The second expression reads the already-updated value 17.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: treating an assignment like an equation that must be solved, or reasoning from the original value after it has been reassigned.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: trace every variable state in a short program, explain update order, and choose a clear representation for the required state.

subtopics.title: types
subtopics.teaching: Teach integers, floating-point values, booleans, characters, and strings through the operations and representations they support. Connect type choice to input parsing and output.
subtopics.worked_example: If a=7 and b="7", a+2 is numeric addition while b+"2" is string concatenation. The same visible digit can represent different data.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: assuming conversion is automatic or harmless, especially when numeric text, integer division, or floating-point precision is involved.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: identify the type of each value, predict type-sensitive operations, and select safe conversions for a coding task.

subtopics.title: input output
subtopics.teaching: Teach the input-process-output contract used by programming judges: parse exactly the required values, compute from them, and emit only the specified output.
subtopics.worked_example: For input `8 5`, a sum program should parse two numbers, calculate 13, and print `13`; adding `Answer:` may violate an exact-output requirement.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: wrong token order, unparsed text, missing multiple test cases, or extra formatting not requested by the problem.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: translate an input/output specification into reliable parsing, processing, and exact output for normal and boundary cases.

subtopics.title: operators
subtopics.teaching: Teach arithmetic, comparison, logical, assignment, and remainder operators by their semantics and precedence. Use parentheses when intent would otherwise be unclear.
subtopics.worked_example: For a=17 and b=5, a%b is 2, a>b is true, and (a+b)*2 is 44. Each operator has a different role in the program's logic.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: confusing `=` with equality, using the wrong logical connector, or overlooking integer-division/remainder behavior in the chosen language.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: select and combine operators correctly, predict results, and explain precedence and type effects in unfamiliar expressions.

subtopics.title: expressions
subtopics.teaching: Teach expressions as evaluated combinations of values and operators. Trace precedence, associativity, conversions, and intermediate values instead of guessing the final result.
subtopics.worked_example: With x=3 and y=4, `x+y*2` is 11, while `(x+y)*2` is 14. Parentheses change the evaluation tree, not merely the formatting.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: evaluating every expression strictly left-to-right or ignoring operand types and implicit conversions.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: evaluate complex expressions accurately, rewrite them without changing meaning, and use intermediate values to debug surprising results.

subtopics.title: conditions
subtopics.teaching: Teach boolean conditions as precise tests that determine a branch. Translate inclusive/exclusive language directly into comparisons and combine predicates deliberately.
subtopics.worked_example: To accept ages from 10 through 15 inclusive, require age>=10 and age<=15. Testing 10, 15, 9, and 16 confirms the boundaries.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: replacing AND with OR, or using `<` where the specification includes the boundary.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: convert natural-language requirements into correct predicates and validate them with boundary and counterexample tests.

subtopics.title: nested conditions
subtopics.teaching: Teach chained and nested decisions as mutually understandable cases. Order tests so every valid input reaches the intended branch and no branch becomes accidentally unreachable.
subtopics.worked_example: For scores below 40, 40–59, and 60+, checking the lower boundary of each range makes 40 pass and 60 distinction without overlap.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: overlapping conditions, unreachable branches, and missing cases caused by inconsistent boundary definitions.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: design complete branch structures, trace every case, and prove that important boundary values receive exactly one intended outcome.

subtopics.title: loops
subtopics.teaching: Teach loops through initialization, condition, body, and update. Students should identify what changes each iteration and why termination is guaranteed.
subtopics.worked_example: A loop with i=1, condition i<=5, and i=i+1 visits 1,2,3,4,5 and stops before 6, so it executes five times.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: off-by-one limits, forgetting the update, or changing the control variable in a way that prevents termination.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: design terminating loops, calculate iteration counts, and trace state changes for unfamiliar inputs.

subtopics.title: iteration patterns
subtopics.teaching: Teach reusable iteration patterns: counting, accumulation, filtering, searching, and building output. Choose the pattern from the task rather than forcing every problem into one template.
subtopics.worked_example: To find the sum of even values in [3,8,5,6], inspect each item once and add only 8 and 6, producing 14.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: initializing an accumulator incorrectly, filtering after instead of before the update, or skipping an element.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: recognize the correct iteration pattern, maintain loop invariants, and verify that every required item is handled exactly once.

subtopics.title: loop tracing
subtopics.teaching: Teach trace tables for loops with columns for iteration, control variables, relevant state, and output. For nested loops, reset inner state whenever the outer iteration changes it.
subtopics.worked_example: For i=1..3 and j=1..2, pairs are (1,1),(1,2),(2,1),(2,2),(3,1),(3,2): six inner executions.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: counting only outer iterations or assuming an inner variable continues from the previous outer iteration when it is reinitialized.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: produce accurate trace tables, predict output and execution counts, and use tracing to locate the first incorrect state.

subtopics.title: functions
subtopics.teaching: Teach functions as named units with a clear input/output contract and limited responsibility. Explain how reusable functions reduce duplication and make tests focused.
subtopics.worked_example: A `square(n)` function returning n*n gives square(4)=16 and square(9)=81; the caller can reuse the same logic without copying it.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: mixing unrelated responsibilities into one function or assuming a function changes external state when it only returns a value.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: define, call, trace, and test focused functions while explaining their contract and side effects.

subtopics.title: parameters
subtopics.teaching: Teach parameters as the local inputs declared by a function and distinguish them from arguments supplied by the caller. Emphasize order, arity, and meaning.
subtopics.worked_example: `area(width,height)` called as `area(5,3)` returns 15; `area(3,5)` is numerically equal here, but argument order matters whenever parameters have different semantics.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: wrong argument order, wrong number of arguments, or assuming a parameter is automatically the same storage location as a caller variable.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: map arguments to parameters correctly and diagnose arity, ordering, and scope mistakes.

subtopics.title: return values
subtopics.teaching: Teach return values as data flowing back to the caller, distinct from printing or other side effects. Show how returned values can participate in larger expressions.
subtopics.worked_example: If `double(n)` returns 2*n, then `total=double(6)+1` gives 13. Printing 12 inside the function would not provide a value for the addition.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: confusing console output with a returned value or expecting statements after `return` to execute.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: trace returned data through composed calls and distinguish computation from presentation.

subtopics.title: scope
subtopics.teaching: Teach local, outer, and nested scope as rules for name visibility. Explain shadowing and why keeping state local reduces accidental coupling.
subtopics.worked_example: If outer x=5 and a function creates local x=10, reading x inside the function can yield 10 while the outer x remains 5 after the call, depending on the language's scope rules.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: assuming equal names always refer to the same variable or that a local variable remains accessible after its scope ends.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: identify which binding a name refers to at each point and predict state changes across function boundaries.

subtopics.title: decomposition
subtopics.teaching: Teach decomposition as splitting a problem along meaningful transformations and responsibilities. Each part should have a clear interface and be independently testable.
subtopics.worked_example: For marks processing, separate parsing, total calculation, average calculation, classification, and output formatting; each stage receives understandable data from the previous one.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: arbitrary fragmentation or functions with overlapping responsibilities that obscure the data flow.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: decompose an unfamiliar coding problem into coherent modules, define their contracts, and explain the complete data flow.

subtopics.title: arrays
subtopics.teaching: Teach arrays as ordered indexed collections. Cover traversal, updates, aggregation, searching, and bounds while keeping index conventions explicit.
subtopics.worked_example: For [4,7,2,9], zero-based indices 0–3 identify the four elements. A loop `i=0` while `i<4` visits each element once.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: confusing human positions with zero-based indices or using the array length as a valid final index.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: traverse, update, search, and aggregate arrays without out-of-range access and with correct boundary reasoning.

subtopics.title: strings
subtopics.teaching: Teach strings as ordered character sequences. Practise indexing, comparison, concatenation, counting, searching, and transformation while distinguishing characters from whole strings.
subtopics.worked_example: For `"VATTAMS"`, the length is 7 and the first character is at index 0 in a zero-based model. Counting vowels requires inspecting each character against the chosen vowel set.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: invalid indices, case mismatches, or assuming string mutation works like array mutation in every language.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: process strings reliably, handle empty/single-character inputs, and produce exact expected text.

subtopics.title: stacks
subtopics.teaching: Teach stacks as last-in-first-out structures with push, pop, and peek. Connect the LIFO invariant to undo, delimiter matching, and depth-first processing.
subtopics.worked_example: Push A, B, C; popping repeatedly returns C, B, A. The newest available item is always removed first.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: treating a stack as FIFO or popping an empty stack without handling underflow.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: simulate stack operations, identify LIFO applications, and handle empty-state transitions safely.

subtopics.title: queues
subtopics.teaching: Teach queues as first-in-first-out structures with enqueue and dequeue. Track front and rear conceptually and handle empty and single-item transitions.
subtopics.worked_example: Enqueue A, B, C; dequeues return A, B, C. This models a service line because the earliest waiting item is processed first.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: reversing insertion/removal order or mishandling the transition from one item to empty.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: simulate FIFO operations accurately and select a queue when arrival order must be preserved.

subtopics.title: maps and sets
subtopics.teaching: Teach maps as key-to-value structures and sets as uniqueness/membership structures. Choose them when direct lookup or duplicate detection is more useful than repeated scanning.
subtopics.worked_example: Insert IDs 101, 102, 101 into a set: the set still contains two unique IDs. A map can associate `101` with its latest score.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: expecting set indexing, assuming map iteration order without a language guarantee, or failing to handle a missing key.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: select the right structure for lookup or uniqueness, simulate updates, and reason about missing keys and duplicates.

subtopics.title: searching
subtopics.teaching: Teach linear search for arbitrary sequences and binary search only when the data is ordered. Compare the work performed by each method and make the precondition for binary search explicit.
subtopics.worked_example: For sorted [2,5,8,11,14,19], searching for 11 with binary search checks the middle region, then narrows to the target. On an unsorted list, linear search is the safe direct method.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: applying binary search to unsorted data, or returning failure before all valid candidates have been examined.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: choose a search method from the data's properties, trace its decisions, handle absent and boundary targets, and justify the choice.

subtopics.title: sorting
subtopics.teaching: Teach sorting as arranging data according to a comparison rule. Contrast simple comparison-based methods conceptually and emphasize preserving the required order and handling duplicates.
subtopics.worked_example: Sorting [7,2,7,4] in ascending order gives [2,4,7,7]. A stable method can preserve the original order of equal records when records carry additional fields.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: sorting in the wrong direction, losing associated data, or assuming duplicate values are automatically removed by sorting.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: select an appropriate sorting approach for the constraints, trace key comparisons or passes, preserve required data, and verify sortedness.

subtopics.title: two pointers
subtopics.teaching: Teach two-pointer techniques for sequences where moving two indices can avoid repeated work. Explain common patterns such as opposite ends and a slow/fast pair, and state the invariant that justifies each movement.
subtopics.worked_example: In sorted [1,3,4,7,9], to find a pair summing to 10, start at both ends: 1+9=10, so the pair is found immediately; otherwise the sum determines which pointer can move safely.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: moving the wrong pointer without using the ordering invariant, or applying the technique when the required ordering/property is absent.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: identify when two pointers reduce repeated scanning, maintain the pointer invariant, and prove that no valid candidate is skipped.

subtopics.title: prefix ideas
subtopics.teaching: Teach prefix sums and related prefix state as a way to answer repeated range questions after one preprocessing pass. Define exactly what each prefix position represents.
subtopics.worked_example: For values [3,5,2,6], prefix sums [3,8,10,16] allow the sum from index 1 through 3 to be obtained as 16-3=13 in a zero-based prefix convention with an initial zero.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: mixing inclusive and exclusive endpoints or forgetting the extra initial zero used by the common prefix-sum formulation.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: construct the correct prefix representation, answer range queries with precise endpoints, and test empty, single-element, and full-range cases.

subtopics.title: recursion basics
subtopics.teaching: Teach recursion through a base case, a smaller recursive subproblem, and progress toward termination. Trace the call stack rather than treating recursion as mysterious repetition.
subtopics.worked_example: A factorial function can define fact(1)=1 and fact(n)=n*fact(n-1). Thus fact(4)=4*3*2*1=24, with the calls returning in reverse order.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: missing or unreachable base cases, recursive calls that do not reduce the problem, or confusing call order with return order.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: identify base and recursive cases, trace the call stack, prove progress toward termination, and recognize when an iterative approach is simpler.

subtopics.title: problem decomposition
subtopics.teaching: Teach decomposition as converting a problem statement into smaller transformations: parse, represent, compute, validate, and output. Name intermediate data explicitly before coding.
subtopics.worked_example: For a frequency task, split the work into reading tokens, normalizing each token, updating a frequency map, and selecting the required result. Each step can be tested separately.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: coding immediately from the story without identifying inputs, outputs, constraints, and intermediate state.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: turn an unfamiliar statement into a sequence of precise subproblems, define their data flow, and identify which part should be solved first.

subtopics.title: constraints
subtopics.teaching: Teach constraints as algorithm-selection evidence. Estimate how input size affects repeated loops, memory use, and whether preprocessing or a faster structure is necessary.
subtopics.worked_example: If n can reach 100,000, an O(n²) pairwise scan may perform about 10 billion comparisons in the worst case, while an O(n log n) strategy is dramatically more practical.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: solving the sample correctly while ignoring the stated maximum input size, causing time or memory failure on judge data.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: read constraints before choosing an approach, estimate growth qualitatively, and reject methods whose resource needs are incompatible with the limits.

subtopics.title: edge cases
subtopics.teaching: Teach edge cases as inputs at or just beyond structural boundaries: empty collections, one item, equal values, minimum/maximum limits, duplicates, and impossible outcomes.
subtopics.worked_example: A maximum-value search over [42] should return 42; an empty-input variant should follow the problem's stated contract rather than assuming an element exists.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: writing logic that only works for the sample's typical case and crashes or returns a wrong result at a boundary.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: systematically derive edge cases from the specification and include them in both mental tracing and targeted tests.

subtopics.title: complexity intuition
subtopics.teaching: Teach time and space complexity as growth estimates rather than exact stopwatch measurements. Compare constant, logarithmic, linear, n log n, and quadratic patterns through their dominant operations.
subtopics.worked_example: For n=1,000, a linear pass is about 1,000 iterations, while a quadratic pairwise process can approach 1,000,000 comparisons. The difference grows rapidly as n increases.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: judging an algorithm only from a small sample or ignoring nested loops and hidden repeated work inside helper functions.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: estimate dominant growth from code structure, compare candidate approaches, and explain why a method should or should not scale to the constraints.

subtopics.title: debugging
subtopics.teaching: Teach debugging as hypothesis-driven diagnosis: reproduce the failure, isolate the smallest failing case, inspect state changes, identify the violated assumption, patch one cause, and retest.
subtopics.worked_example: If a sum is too large only when the first element is negative, test a one-element negative case and inspect accumulator initialization before changing unrelated loop logic.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: changing several lines at once or fixing the visible output without identifying the state or assumption that caused the error.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: localize a bug using traces and minimal tests, explain its root cause, apply a targeted fix, and confirm that old cases still pass.

subtopics.title: tracing
subtopics.teaching: Teach code tracing as executing statements mentally or with a trace table while recording only state relevant to the output. Follow branches, loop updates, calls, and returns in order.
subtopics.worked_example: For x=2, then repeat three times with x=x+2, the recorded states are 2,4,6,8; the final value is 8 and the intermediate states explain how it was reached.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: skipping a branch or loop iteration because the final result seems obvious, especially when a variable is changed in multiple places.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: trace unfamiliar code line by line at the relevant state changes and use the trace to justify the exact output.

subtopics.title: test cases
subtopics.teaching: Teach test cases as deliberate evidence: include normal, boundary, duplicate, empty/singleton, and invalid/impossible cases when the specification permits them. Each test should target a possible failure mode.
subtopics.worked_example: For a function that returns the larger of two numbers, test (5,3), (3,5), (4,4), and the allowed minimum values rather than testing only one ordering.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: relying on one happy-path sample or choosing tests that all exercise the same branch.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: design a compact but high-value test set that covers requirements, boundaries, and likely implementation mistakes.

subtopics.title: failure diagnosis
subtopics.teaching: Teach diagnosis by separating syntax/build errors, runtime failures, wrong-answer logic, and resource failures. Read the symptom first, then trace backward to the smallest violated assumption.
subtopics.worked_example: If the program compiles but fails only on large inputs, inspect algorithmic complexity and memory growth before rewriting basic syntax.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: treating every failure as a coding typo or changing the algorithm without confirming what category of failure occurred.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: classify failures correctly, connect symptoms to likely causes, and produce a targeted fix supported by a reproducing case.

subtopics.title: boundary conditions
subtopics.teaching: Teach boundary conditions as the exact transition points where loop limits, ranges, indices, or validity rules change. Make inclusive/exclusive choices explicit in code.
subtopics.worked_example: For an array of length n, the last zero-based index is n-1. A loop `i<n` visits valid positions; `i<=n` attempts one invalid position.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: using a mathematically correct-looking boundary that does not match the programming representation.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: identify every relevant boundary, test values immediately below/at/above it, and implement limits without off-by-one errors.

subtopics.title: verification
subtopics.teaching: Teach verification as independently checking that a program satisfies the specification, not merely that it produces the expected sample. Use invariants, alternative calculations, and adversarial tests.
subtopics.worked_example: After sorting an array, verify that every adjacent pair is nondecreasing and that the output contains the same multiset of values as the input; both properties support correctness.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: confirming only the final sample output or using the same flawed reasoning to verify the program that produced the result.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: state a correctness property, test it independently, and explain evidence that the implementation preserves the required behavior.

subtopics.title: simulation
subtopics.teaching: Teach simulation as maintaining program state exactly as the problem describes each event or operation. Identify state variables, event order, and transition rules before coding.
subtopics.worked_example: For a counter starting at 10, events +3, -2, +5 produce states 10→13→11→16. Applying events in a different order changes the result, so ordering is part of the specification.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: skipping an event, applying simultaneous-looking operations in the wrong order, or updating a state variable from stale rather than current data.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: translate event rules into deterministic state transitions, trace every event, and validate the final state against small hand-worked cases.

subtopics.title: text processing
subtopics.teaching: Teach text processing through tokenization, normalization, character scanning, and exact output rules. Decide whether case, whitespace, punctuation, and Unicode distinctions matter from the specification.
subtopics.worked_example: To count vowels in `Code`, scan C-o-d-e and count o and e, giving 2. If the task is case-insensitive, normalize case before testing characters.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: accidentally counting punctuation, mishandling spaces, or applying case-sensitive logic when the specification treats letters uniformly.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: transform and inspect text according to explicit rules, handle empty and whitespace-heavy inputs, and preserve required output formatting.

subtopics.title: mathematical coding
subtopics.teaching: Teach mathematical coding by translating a mathematical definition into integer-safe program operations. Check divisibility, overflow, rounding, and boundary behavior rather than copying formulas blindly.
subtopics.worked_example: To compute the sum of the first n positive integers, use n*(n+1)/2 when the language and constraints safely support the intermediate product; for large values, choose a representation that avoids overflow.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: floating-point arithmetic for exact integer answers, incorrect operator precedence, or overflow before division reduces the value.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: convert definitions into robust code, validate with small cases, and account for numeric limits and exactness.

subtopics.title: data handling
subtopics.teaching: Teach data handling as a pipeline: parse records, choose an appropriate representation, transform or aggregate them, and emit the required result. Preserve associations between related fields.
subtopics.worked_example: For records `(id,score)`, a map from id to score supports direct lookup while an array of records preserves input order; the choice depends on whether lookup or ordering is required.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: losing field associations, assuming input order is sorted, or converting values to text when later arithmetic is required.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: choose representations from access needs, preserve data integrity through transformations, and verify both values and required ordering.

subtopics.title: challenge problems
subtopics.teaching: Teach championship challenge solving as a disciplined cycle: understand the statement, derive the invariant or key observation, choose an algorithm, prove it on representative cases, implement, and stress-test boundaries.
subtopics.worked_example: For a duplicate-detection task, a set provides a direct membership invariant: before inserting a value, membership tells whether it has already appeared. The approach avoids repeated pairwise comparisons.
subtopics.pitfall: Pitfall: coding the first plausible pattern without proving why it covers all cases, especially when constraints require a less obvious optimization.
subtopics.mastery: Mastery: independently derive a viable approach for unfamiliar problems, justify correctness and complexity, implement cleanly, and verify with adversarial tests.
